messages:
nate: Quick follow-up from the RFC meeting — we need a call on where to attach billing/cost keys for accurate attribution. Options: propagate billing_key on every span, only root trace, or attach during ingest enrichment handshake. Pros/cons? :thinking:

li: my 2c: attaching at span-level gives best accuracy for shard-level billing but high cardinality. root-only keeps cardinality low but loses subrequest cost split.

sophie: Agree with li. Also think we should consider sampling interaction. If we sample at tail, root-only loses per-span attribution on sampled spans.

aj: What about hybrid: attach billing_key on root + allow span override when explicitly set by SDK (e.g., proxied requests). That keeps common-case small.

nate: hybrid sounds reasonable. Edge cases: async fan-out where downstream services run under different customers — need overrides.

li: Example schema we discussed:
```
trace.attributes: {service, env, trace_id, billing_key?, org_id?}
span.attributes: {op, duration_ms, billing_key?}
```
If SDK sets span.billing_key it overrides trace.billing_key for that span.

sophie: We also need to agree on retention & cardinality caps. Proposal: keep billing_key as low-cardinality tag (whitelisted), drop unrecognized high-card tags at ingest with metrics on drop rate.

ingest-bot: Deploy queued: enrich-handshake v1.2 scheduled 02:00 UTC — adds explicit billing_key header passthrough. :robot_face:

aj: Two operational flags: 1) per-tenant cardinality cap 2) tagging whitelist. We should gate rollout behind a small pilot.

nate: Can we document a migration plan? steps: SDK + proxy changes -> ingest handshake -> enrichment layer -> rollout with pilot -> enable sampling-aware backfill. Who volunteers to draft?

li: I'll write the pilot plan and a short migration doc. I'll post a PR in infra-observability by EOD tomorrow.

sophie: I'll own the runtime guardrails (caps/metrics) and add dashboards for drop-rate + attribution coverage.

nate: Perfect. Follow-up sync Friday 10:00 PT. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
